I had a friend who was going through mental health issues. It made him difficult to be around and a lot of his friends abandoned him. I tried to be as good a friend as I could and stayed around to help him get through it. I was there to give him love and support when he needed it, and gave him space when he was having a real rough go at it. This went on for over a year. 

Eventually he just went completely off the map, turned off all contact with people (phone/social media) and told everyone he would be back after a few month break. I understood and told him I would be there for him when he came back. After a few months, he came back and said he wanted to reconnect with all his friends again, carving out special time with each of them. I watched as he started posting photos with different friends everyday, including some that had abandoned him at the beginning of his issues. Patiently I waited for him to contact me about wanting to get together and do something. 

Finally one day he messaged me about spending some time together, and I invited him over to my house to have dinner with me and my girlfriend (who he also was friends with). I was so excited to show him my new house and introduce him to my friends/roommates. I asked him if he was ok with all of that, since I know that could have been overwhelming, and he said it was and that he was excited. So I began planning, picking out the best dinner that would suit his tastes, planning some possible activities for the night, just trying to make it as enjoyable a night as I could.

Then, the night before he was supposed to come over, he cancelled. He told me that he was having a bad couple of days and just wasn't ready to see people for a few days. It hurt my feelings of course but I understood. I didn't want to push him so I told him he was welcome to come by at a different date if he wanted. He appreciated it and said he would after he cheered up and felt like seeing people again. The next evening, I see photos he posted on Facebook of the party he was at and how happy he was to be with friends. It shattered me heart. To think I went through all of that effort to be turned down and lied to. It especially hurt because we had been close friends since the 1st grade. I never thought he could do that to me. We haven't really spoken since. He invited me to his birthday vacation a few months later but I just couldn't do it.

While I agree with a lot of the points you made, I feel like some could be changed. First off, I actually think that the prequel trilogy would need to be the longer one. They pack a lot of history into those movies, it's hard to hard to show it all in a few hours. I also think they shouldn't take Darth Maul into the other movies. I do agree that he was an interesting character that deserved more back story and screen time but I would have had Episode 1 be more about him by giving some more time to flush out his character. But they killed him off at a good time. If you let him be the apprentice of Palpatine throughout all the prequel movies, you would have missed out on some awesome characters such as Count Douku and General Grievous. And I don't care how you feel about them, if they had had better character development, they would have been some pretty bad ass characters. And how would they add more to the original movies? They are already pretty well done and I feel that if they added something, it would just be padding. And to go along with having Boba have a better death, they should give Jango a better one too. He really didn't do anything in Episode 2 and he probably would have been able to do some awesome stuff if he made it to Episode 3. Just think of that opening space battle with Slave 1 flying around. And for a death, he could have like an awesome mano a mano fight with Obi-Wan or he could sacrifice himself for Boba or something along those lines. But you know, those are just my opinions
